Explanation:

  • • The CDC (Centers for Disease Control and Prevention) defines AIDS based on the presence of certain opportunistic infections or cancers. Melanoma, while serious, does not meet the criteria to be classified as an AIDS-defining condition.
  • • Incorrect Options: A) Kaposi sarcoma Correctly classified as an AIDS-defining cancer. Caused by HHV-8, it is especially common in advanced HIV disease and is one of the first recognized AIDS-associated cancers.
  • • B) Cervical cancer Invasive cervical cancer is an AIDS-defining illness. It is caused by persistent HPV infection and is particularly aggressive in HIV-positive individuals.
  • • C) Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma (NHL) Certain types of NHL (especially high-grade B-cell lymphomas like primary CNS lymphoma) are considered AIDS-defining conditions due to their strong association with HIV-related immunosuppression.
